title: Articles: check yourself
intro: 10 tasks: el, la, un, una, al and del, and when to use no article.

items.explanation: A + el joins into al: voy al médico.
optionNotes: A and el always join into al.
Médico is masculine here: el médico.

items.context: It's the teacher's book and the doctor's car.
items.text: Es el libro {{1}} profesor y el coche {{2}} médica.
items.explanation: De + el = del (del profesor); de + la does not change (de la médica).

items.prompt: ___ niños son muy curiosos. (children in general)
items.explanation: Things or people in general take the definite article: los niños.
optionNotes: Unos niños would be “some children”, not children in general.

items.explanation: Pregunta is feminine singular and new: una pregunta.
optionNotes: La would mean a specific question already known.

items.explanation: When you speak to someone directly, the title has no article: Hola, señora Ruiz, ¿cómo está?

items.source: I'm going to the movies. (voy = I'm going)

items.explanation: No article before a job on its own: es médico.

items.prompt: ___ agua de este río está muy fría. (está = is)
items.explanation: Agua starts with a stressed a-, so the singular article is el, although agua is feminine (fría).
optionNotes: A feminine noun with a stressed a- takes el in the singular.

items.context: The children are from the city.
answers: Los niños son de la ciudad.
items.explanation: Los niños (the children) is the subject; de la ciudad has no contraction because ciudad is feminine.

items.prompt: Match the article with the noun.
items.explanation: El problema and unos días are masculine; las manos and una canción are feminine.
